findings.text: follow-on: row r-20260918T201949355073-nia-limited-boundary-touches-wall-2 stores the three failure ids under a new top-level 'failures' key that no reader consumes. The ledger's declared record fields (reckon/ledger.py:107-162) enumerate the row keys and 'failures' is not among them, so the ids are data only: the source followup asked that the row 'preserve the three failure IDs rather than classifying them away', but a gate reading the ledger cannot see them. The canonical home for a gate's failures is the suite observation (baseline_suite/after_suite failure_ids, reckon/ledger.py:275) rather than an undeclared row key.

follow-on: the 'executable argv' claim in the done_when is only half met. gate_check.command is stored as a JSON list, but reckon's canonical gate-check normaliser (_normalized_gate_check, reckon/ledger.py:241) coerces any command with str(), so the same list read back through the ledger writer becomes the unexecutable Python-repr string "['env', 'TMPDIR=/tmp', 'srun', ...]". I verified this by running _normalized_gate_check on the stored list. The row is correct in the committed file (written textually, not through the writer), but a re-normalisation by the ledger does not round-trip the argv shape it records.

follow-on: the write-path guard the source followup (f-fsa-wall-ledger-gate-integrity-full) requires — a gate status that must agree with exit_status before promotion — is not added by this node, which was to correct the two rows only. As delivered, 8 rows still carry gate 'passed' with gate_check.exit_status != 0 (r-20260908T031258319849-pfs-centroid-radius-report exit 1, r-20260919T071103282439-review-of-nia-limited-boundary-touches-wall-2 exit 1, r-20260915T055602091466-cca-newton-krylov-iteration-count exit 1, and five more), and the promotion writer refuses a passing gate only when the check is missing or malformed, never when exit_status disagrees with the verdict. The defect class this node repaired in two rows remains unguarded in the writer.
